title: Anthropic IPO: What It Means for Traders and How to Buy ANT From India
summary: ANT priced at $83, first traded at $111.50 and closed at $97.17. See what the Anthropic IPO means for traders and how Indians can buy after listing.
body_markdown:
The Anthropic IPO is the Nasdaq listing of Anthropic, the company behind Claude, under the ticker ANT. The shares were priced at $83, opened at $111.50 and closed the first day at $97.17.


Indian residents can buy ANT after listing, through a US broker or investing platform that accepts Indian residents and offers the stock. India was outside Anthropic’s designated retail IPO offering, so Indian buyers pay the market price, not the $83 IPO price.

## IPO Price vs First Trade: Who Made Money on Day One?


An IPO allotment and a purchase after listing happen at different stages. Investors who get an IPO allotment buy at the final offer price. Everyone else buys at whatever the market charges once trading starts.


ANT’s first public trade came at 11:48 AM ET at $111.50, which was 34.3% above the IPO price. It closed at $97.17, well off its high of around $115.

### How to Buy ANT Shares From India


-


**Open an account:** you need a[US stock account with an Indian platform](https://algotest.in/blog/best-brokers-to-invest-in-us-stocks-from-india/) that lists ANT and accepts Indian residents.


-


**Fund it under LRS:** the RBI’s Liberalised Remittance Scheme lets each resident individual send up to $250,000 per financial year for eligible transactions, including overseas investments. This is your overall LRS limit, not a separate limit just for stocks.


-


**Plan for TCS:** it’s charged at 20% on remittances above ₹10 lakh. If you send ₹12 lakh in a year, TCS applies only to the ₹2 lakh above the threshold, which works out to ₹40,000. You can claim it as a credit when you file your income tax return.


-


**Place your order during US market hours:** the[US market opens at 8:00 PM IST](https://algotest.in/blog/us-market-opening-time-in-india/) in November.


Platforms differ on brokerage, FX markup and withdrawal fees. You can[compare two popular US investing apps](https://algotest.in/blog/vested-vs-indmoney-for-us-stocks/) side by side and read up on[the tax rules for US stocks](https://algotest.in/blog/how-to-invest-in-us-stocks-from-india/) before you send money.

## What the Anthropic IPO Means for Traders


-


**Direct AI exposure:** traders can now own a frontier AI lab directly instead of relying on proxies. Amazon will own about 15% of Anthropic and Google about 14% after the IPO.


-


**Big early swings:** the stock went from 34% above its IPO price at the first trade to 17% above it at the close, all on day one. New listings often keep swinging while the market settles on a price.


-


**Possible index inclusion:** Bloomberg reported that ANT is on track to join the Nasdaq 100 on 21 December, if it meets the eligibility rules. Treat it as a date to watch, not a trade signal.


-


**A record listing:** the Associated Press called it the largest public stock offering on record, so it will stay a reference point for future mega IPOs.

## Is There an Anthropic IPO GMP?


No. GMP (grey market premium) is an unofficial price that Indian IPO shares trade at before listing, and US IPOs like ANT have no such market.


The closest signal was pre-IPO perpetual futures on crypto venues. On Hyperliquid, a contract tracking one Anthropic share closed at $102.87 on 10 November. Treat that as a sentiment gauge, not a price guide.

### FAQs


#### Can Indians buy Anthropic shares?


Yes, after listing. Eligible Indian residents can buy ANT through a US broker or investing platform that accepts Indian residents and offers the stock, using the LRS route. India was not part of the designated retail IPO offering.


#### What was the Anthropic IPO price?


Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its $70 to $78 range. Trading started on Nasdaq on 19 November 2026.


#### Is buying the Anthropic IPO a good idea?


It depends on your time frame, risk limits and how much AI exposure you already hold. Past mega IPOs have fallen 20% to 50% below their first-day close within six months, so plan your exit before you buy. This article is for education, not investment advice.


#### When could ANT join the Nasdaq-100?


Bloomberg reported that ANT is on track to join the Nasdaq 100 on 21 December 2026, provided it meets the index’s eligibility rules.
